subject: EdgeScale data-use commitments, EU residency & derivative rights
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara@edgescale.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: guarantees on model improvement + EU residency options

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this early look. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot and need to lock down a few privacy items before procurement can move forward:

- Strong 'no-derivative' / 'no-training' commitment for any customer-supplied prompts/responses (including embeddings) — we need language that blocks use for model improvement.
- Clarity on ownership: EdgeScale needs explicit confirmation that prompt/response output remains our IP and is exportable.
- Subprocessor residency: any subprocessors processing our EU customer data must be EU-resident or we require logs/evidence showing EU-only handling.
- A workable evidence path (SFTP export or signed attestation) to prove residency for initial security review.

Can Redwood provide contract language + an evidence pack (subprocessor list + attestations)? If you can also indicate whether a managed EU-only SFTP of logs is possible for our DPA, that would help speed approval.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants to close by the end of next week.

Best,
Sara
Sara Park
Legal & Compliance, EdgeScale
attachments: none
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Inquiry: guarantees on model improvement + EU residency options

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, and I've attached a proposed redline to the DPA for your review (Redwood_DPA_redline_20260526.pdf).

1) No-training / No-derivative: We can commit in the DPA that Customer Data (defined as prompts, attachments, and model responses tied to your tenant) will not be used to improve or train Redwood models or any third-party models. Proposed language in the redline uses the phrase: "Customer Data will not be used for model training, evaluation, or derivation of model weights."

2) Prompt/response IP: We will include an explicit output ownership clause confirming customer retains rights to prompts and generated responses; Redwood grants a limited right to operate the service only.

3) Subprocessors & residency: We maintain a subprocessor list and can provide EU-only processing options for customer data. For the pilot we can offer either (a) EU region hosting for all production request processing, or (b) dedicated SFTP export of logs/artefacts hosted in an EU region on a weekly cadence.

4) Evidence pack: see attached 'subprocessor_attestation_20260527.pdf' (we'll provide a signed attestation and an inventory of subprocessors). If you'd like, we can scope an additional operational attestation (signed) that certifies EU-only handling for the pilot.

Karthik — can you confirm whether the SFTP export option is feasible from the infra side for a pilot (EU region) and typical lead time?

We can iterate quickly on your DPA comments — please send your markups.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Sara Park <sara@edgescale.io>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 08:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Inquiry: guarantees on model improvement + EU residency options

Vanessa — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from legal/procurement after reviewing the redline:

- Definition: we need a tight definition for "Customer Data" to avoid telemetry/diagnostic leakages being classified as "non-customer" and used for training. For example, if prompt text is present in logs for debugging, we need assurance it's still covered by no-train.
- Service telemetry: please clarify what you consider "aggregated telemetry" vs. "diagnostic logs" — procurement treats any content containing prompt snippets as potential PD.
- Subprocessor proof: we asked for a signed attestation and also a mechanism for us to pull logs to our own EU SFTP (read-only) for audit. Is a weekly secure SFTP push feasible?

I've attached our annotated DPA (EdgeScale_DPA_comments.docx) with suggested edits. If Redwood can provide a short, signed attestation that states: "Redwood will not use Customer Data for model training, and all subprocessors processing EdgeScale EU data will be bound by the same restriction and process EU-only handling in the listed subprocessors" — that will satisfy our InfoSec gating.

Tom (cc) will handle the procurement form and DocuSign once we have the attestation.

Best,
Sara
attachments: EdgeScale_DPA_comments.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@edgescale.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 11:40:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Inquiry: guarantees on model improvement + EU residency options

Sara / Vanessa — looping in legal wording we can commit to for the pilot. High-level summary and exact clauses below; attached is the short attestation and subprocessor inventory we'll sign (subprocessor_attestation_20260527.pdf).

Proposed commitments we can put in the DPA (pilot scope):
- No-Training Clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Data (defined as any data submitted to the Service by the Customer, including prompts, files, responses, embeddings, and any derived metadata that could be used to reconstruct original content) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models."
- Telemetry carve: "Redwood may collect aggregated, anonymized telemetry for service health and capacity planning that does not contain Customer Data or any fragments capable of re-identifying Customer Data. Diagnostic logs that contain Customer Data will be treated as Customer Data and handled only in accordance with this DPA."
- Subprocessors: All subprocessors will be contractually bound to the DPA terms and the no-training commitment. For EU-region customers, Redwood will (a) route processing through EU-located infrastructure; and (b) provide a weekly SFTP export (read-only) of request logs to a customer-owned EU SFTP endpoint for audit.

Operational notes: lead time for the SFTP export option is typically 5 business days to configure and verify host keys. If EdgeScale requires continuous sync instead of weekly exports, we can evaluate Dedicated/Private deployment options (longer lead time and additional costs).

We've prepared the signed attestation stub and the current subprocessors inventory in the attached PDF. If the language above matches your legal team's needs, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet with the DPA redline + attestation.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Counsel (on behalf of Redwood Legal)
